title: From Career Goal to Transition Plan
summary: Learn how to turn a career direction into a practical transition plan that identifies real requirements, possible pathways, next actions, deadlines, and sources that need verification.
objectives: Explain the difference between a career goal and a transition plan.
Identify major categories that belong in a transition plan.
Separate confirmed next steps from possibilities that still need verification.

vocab.def: A working plan that connects a learner's current position to a specific education, training, work-based learning, employment, or other next step.
A specific action that moves a learner toward a defined goal.
A condition that must be satisfied for a particular program, credential, opportunity, training route, or other next step.
Checking important pathway information through an appropriate authoritative or trusted source.

sections.heading: A goal tells you where you want to go
sections.body: A career goal can describe an occupation, field, training direction, or next experience. It gives direction, but it does not yet explain how you will get there.

sections.heading: A transition plan explains what happens next
sections.body: A useful transition plan identifies requirements, current preparation, remaining gaps, possible routes, deadlines, contacts, documents, opportunities, and concrete next actions.

sections.heading: Different routes may lead toward the same goal
sections.body: Depending on the career and learner, possible routes may include apprenticeship, community college, technical school, university, work-based learning, further training, or entry-level employment.

sections.heading: Possible is not the same as confirmed
sections.body: A pathway should not be treated as available, approved, or guaranteed until the relevant requirements, eligibility, provider information, deadlines, and actual opportunities have been verified.

practice.prompt: A learner writes, 'I want to become an electrician.' Is that a complete transition plan?
practice.answer: No. It is a career goal. A transition plan still needs verified requirements, possible routes, current preparation, gaps, deadlines, and concrete next actions.

practice.prompt: A learner hears that a local apprenticeship may be available next year. Should it be listed as confirmed?
practice.answer: Not until the actual program, requirements, availability, and application information are verified.

quiz.question: What makes a transition plan stronger than a career goal alone?
options: It connects the goal to verified requirements, routes, deadlines, and specific next actions
It automatically enrolls the learner in a program
quiz.answer: It connects the goal to verified requirements, routes, deadlines, and specific next actions

lab.objective: Choose a simulated or learner-selected career direction and draft the first transition-plan outline: goal, possible routes, requirements to verify, current preparation, known gaps, and one immediate next action.

reflectionPrompt: What is the difference between saying what you want to do and knowing the next verified action that moves you toward it?
